what: Weyerhaeuser owns about 10 million acres of American timberland and the mills that turn those trees into lumber and engineered wood. It is structured as a REIT.
customers: Homebuilders and building products distributors, plus buyers of land for development and conservation.
money: lumber, oriented strand board and engineered wood
logs sold from its own forests
Real Estate, Energy and Natural Resources
land sales, mineral rights and carbon projects
moat: The land itself. Ten million acres of productive timberland cannot be assembled again, and the trees keep growing in value whether or not they are cut this year.
risks: Lumber prices are volatile and set almost entirely by housing starts
Revenue fell from $10.2B to $6.9B as the housing boom ended
$5.7B of debt against $464M of cash in a cyclical business
opportunities: Analysts see about 36% upside, the widest gap among timber REITs
Trees left standing in a weak market keep growing, so a downturn postpones value rather than destroying it
Carbon credits and land leased for solar and wind add income that does not depend on lumber prices
watch: United States housing starts and the realised price per thousand board feet of lumber.
